grammar.title: Articles: a / an / the / no article

explain.en: Use a / an for one thing when we mention it for the first time. Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
explain.ar: نستخدم a أو an مع اسم مفرد معدود عند ذكره لأول مرة. نستخدم a قبل صوت ساكن (a book) و an قبل صوت متحرك (an apple, an hour).

explain.en: Use the when the listener knows which thing we mean, when it is the only one, or when we mention it again.
explain.ar: نستخدم the عندما يكون الشيء معروفًا للمستمع، أو وحيدًا (the sun)، أو عندما نكرر ذكره.

grammar.title: Prepositions of time and place: at / on / in

explain.en: Use at for exact times and small points, on for days, dates and surfaces, and in for months, years, seasons, parts of the day and enclosed places.
explain.ar: نستخدم at مع الساعة والنقاط المحددة، و on مع الأيام والتواريخ والأسطح، و in مع الأشهر والسنوات والفصول وأجزاء اليوم والأماكن المغلقة.

grammar.title: have / has, was / were, there is / there are

explain.en: Use has with he, she, it and have with I, you, we, they. Use was with I, he, she, it and were with you, we, they.
explain.ar: نستخدم has مع he/she/it و have مع I/you/we/they. ونستخدم was مع I/he/she/it و were مع you/we/they.

explain.en: Use there is with singular and uncountable nouns, and there are with plural nouns.
explain.ar: نستخدم there is مع المفرد وغير المعدود، و there are مع الجمع.

explain.en: Uncountable nouns (milk, water, homework) take is: Is there any water?

explain.en: Use the present simple for habits, facts and timetables: every day, always, usually, never.

explain.en: Use the present continuous (am / is / are + verb-ing) for actions happening now or around now: now, at the moment, look!, listen!

explain.en: Use the past simple for a finished action in the past: yesterday, last week, in 2020.

explain.en: Use the past continuous (was / were + verb-ing) for a longer action in progress. A shorter action (past simple) interrupts it with when; use while for the long action.

grammar.title: Present perfect: for, since, already, yet, just, ever

explain.en: Form: have / has + past participle. We use it for experiences, for results now, and for actions that started in the past and continue until now.
explain.ar: التكوين: have/has + التصريف الثالث للفعل. نستخدمه للخبرات، وللنتائج الحالية، ولأحداث بدأت في الماضي وما زالت مستمرة.

grammar.title: Quantifiers: some, any, much, many, a lot of, few, little

explain.en: Many and a few go with countable nouns (books). Much and a little go with uncountable nouns (water). Use a lot of with both.
explain.ar: نستخدم many وa few مع المعدود (books)، و much وa little مع غير المعدود (water)، و a lot of مع النوعين.

explain.en: Use some in positive sentences and offers; use any in negatives and questions. Few / little (without a) mean almost none.
explain.ar: نستخدم some في الإثبات والعرض، و any في النفي والسؤال. وكلمتا few / little بدون a تعنيان قليل جدًا تقريبًا لا يوجد.

explain.en: Some verbs are followed by -ing: enjoy, finish, mind, keep, avoid, suggest. Some verbs are followed by to + verb: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, would like.

explain.en: After a preposition use -ing (good at, interested in). Use to + verb to show purpose.

grammar.title: Modal verbs: should, must, have to, can, could

explain.en: Modal verbs are followed by the base verb (no to, no -s). Should gives advice; must / have to show obligation; mustn't shows prohibition; don't have to means it is not necessary.
explain.ar: بعد الأفعال الناقصة نستخدم الفعل الأصلي (بدون to أو s). should للنصيحة، و must / have to للإلزام، و mustn't للمنع، و don't have to تعني ليس ضروريًا.

phrasal.meaning: to support sb or show that sth is true
phrasal.ex: My friends backed me up at the meeting.

phrasal.meaning: to make a copy of computer files
phrasal.ex: Always back up your photos before you update the phone.

phrasal.meaning: to look after a child until he or she is an adult
phrasal.ex: Her grandmother brought her up.

phrasal.meaning: to meet or find sb/sth by chance
phrasal.ex: I came across an old photo in the drawer.

phrasal.meaning: to take action to solve a problem or handle sth
phrasal.ex: The teacher dealt with the problem quickly.

phrasal.meaning: to get information by asking or studying
phrasal.ex: Let us find out what time the bus leaves.

phrasal.meaning: to give sth free to sb
phrasal.ex: We gave away our old toys to the charity shop.

phrasal.meaning: to proceed or begin
phrasal.ex: Please go ahead and start the presentation.

phrasal.meaning: to leave a place or leave home for a time
phrasal.ex: The family went away for the weekend.

phrasal.meaning: to return to a place
phrasal.ex: I want to go back to Muscat in the summer.

phrasal.meaning: to enter a place
phrasal.ex: The teacher knocked and then went in.

phrasal.meaning: to talk about or explain sth in detail
phrasal.ex: I will not go into the details now.

phrasal.meaning: to start or stop using the internet
phrasal.ex: I go online every evening to check my emails.

phrasal.meaning: to end a phone call
phrasal.ex: He said goodbye and hung up.

phrasal.meaning: to move or do sth more quickly
phrasal.ex: Hurry up, or we will be late for school.

phrasal.meaning: to move or progress at the same speed as sb/sth
phrasal.ex: It is hard to keep up with new technology.

phrasal.meaning: to enter a computer system with a password
phrasal.ex: Log in to the school website to see your marks.

phrasal.meaning: to leave a computer system
phrasal.ex: Do not forget to log out of your account.

phrasal.meaning: to take care of sb or sth
phrasal.ex: Huda looks after her little sister after school.

phrasal.meaning: to try to find sb or sth
phrasal.ex: I am looking for my keys.

phrasal.meaning: to visit sb for a short time
phrasal.ex: I will look in on my grandmother on the way home.

phrasal.meaning: to be careful
phrasal.ex: Look out! The floor is wet.

phrasal.meaning: to walk around a place and see it, or turn your head

phrasal.meaning: to read or check sth quickly
phrasal.ex: She looked through her notes before the exam.

phrasal.meaning: to find information in a book or on a computer
phrasal.ex: Look up the new word in your dictionary.

phrasal.meaning: to invent sth, such as a story or an excuse
phrasal.ex: He made up a story about a talking camel.

phrasal.meaning: to connect a device to the electricity supply
phrasal.ex: Plug the charger in, please.

phrasal.meaning: to escape from a place
phrasal.ex: The cat ran away when it saw the dog.

phrasal.meaning: to use all of sth so that none is left
phrasal.ex: We have run out of paper.

phrasal.meaning: to move up or down a screen to read or look
phrasal.ex: I scroll through the news every morning.

phrasal.meaning: to start a business or prepare equipment

phrasal.meaning: to put your name on a list or join a course
phrasal.ex: Many students signed up for the science club.

phrasal.meaning: to press a switch to start or stop electric power
phrasal.ex: Please switch off the lights when you leave.

phrasal.meaning: to get rid of sth you do not want

phrasal.meaning: to arrive or appear

phrasal.meaning: to lower the sound or heat, or to refuse sth
